properties.name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
properties.note: Fortified zone established by the 1953 armistice.
properties.construction: Fortified zone: barbed-wire fences, minefields and guard posts; not a continuous wall
properties.initiated_by: 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement (UN Command, North Korea, China)
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; barrier extent not checked)
properties.purpose: Military buffer under the 1953 armistice.

properties.name: Berlin Wall
properties.note: Encircled West Berlin until November 1989. Drawn line covers only the surviving segments found in OpenStreetMap.
properties.construction: Concrete wall (prefabricated concrete slabs) with watchtowers and a cleared 'death strip'
properties.geometry_quality: partial (surviving segments traced in OpenStreetMap; the full route is not mapped)
properties.purpose: Officially 'anti-fascist protection'; in practice stopped emigration from the GDR.

properties.name: Moroccan Western Sahara Wall (Berm)
properties.note: Built in six stages, 1980–1987 (construction ended April 1987). Article gives a total length of 2,500–2,700 km (2,600 km used). The line shows the main route only, from the article's example point at 23.26 N, 16.04 W (Guerguerat is named as the start but not located) through Tichla, Guelta Zemmur, Smara and Haouza to a northern fort. Anti-personnel mines dropped by Moroccan aircraft, number not given.
properties.construction: Sand-dune earth berm (successive dune lines) with trenches, barbed wire, electronic sensors and fortified posts; mined along much of its length
properties.initiated_by: Government of Morocco (built with French technicians)
properties.geometry_quality: traced (OpenStreetMap contributors, 229 ways; sections may be incomplete)
properties.purpose: Stated: defence against the Polisario Front.

properties.name: India–Bangladesh border fence
properties.note: Construction started in the late 1980s, still being extended.
properties.construction: Mainly barbed-wire fence; some sections with floodlights and patrol roads
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; river sections and fenced extent not checked)
properties.cost: ≈ $1.62 billion / ≈ €1.19 billion in 2024 prices. Original: Sanctioned phases: about Rs 1,050–1,060 crore (Phase I), Rs 4,394–4,405 crore (Phase II), Rs 884 crore (Phase III). Sum about Rs 6,330–6,350 crore (own arithmetic; phases partly overlap). [sum of sanctioned phases (Rs 6,340 crore), mostly 2009–2014; year assumed 2012]
properties.security_technology: Not documented in the sources beyond fence and roads.
properties.purpose: Stated: border management against illegal crossing and smuggling (Indian government).

properties.name: Ceuta border fence
properties.note: Official length about 8.2 km (Infobae, 2023); older figures about 7.5–8.4 km. Concertina wire replaced from late 2019. Exact alignment from Spanish records not found.
properties.construction: Fence 2.5 m high (1993), raised to 3 m (1995) and 6 m (2005); double fence with concertina wire, replaced from late 2019
properties.geometry_quality: traced (OpenStreetMap, 7 ways; government trace not published, sections may be incomplete)
properties.cost: ≈ $15.8 million (2005); 11.4 million (2019); 30.0 million (2018–2026 spend) / ≈ €11.7 million (2005); 10.0 million (2019); 28.7 million (2018–2026 spend) in 2024 prices. Original: €7.9 million for the 2005 raise (Público, 2014); €8.3 million for the 2019 concertina upgrade; Interior spent over €26.6 million 2018–2026 (The Objective, 2026) [spend figures are approximate; mid-period years used]
properties.maintenance_cost: ≈ $1.3 million a year / ≈ €1.1 million a year in 2024 prices. Original: €9.24 million over 2015–2024, about €0.92 million a year (Spanish government figures reported by The Objective) [annual average, 2020 prices]
properties.purpose: Stated: stop irregular migration.

properties.name: US–Mexico border barrier
properties.note: Expanded after the 2006 Secure Fence Act and again from 2017.
properties.construction: Steel bollard fence (primary barrier), with secondary barrier in places; older mesh and vehicle barriers replaced
properties.initiated_by: US government (Secure Fence Act 2006 and later programmes)
properties.cost: ≈ $46.55 billion / ≈ €41.20 billion in 2024 prices. Original: Program appropriation of $46.55 billion (Public Law 119-21, through Sept 2029), covering barriers, cameras, sensors, roads and maintenance. Per-mile figures: CBP's older estimate about $6.5 million per mile; recent contracts reported near $20 million per mile (not official). [2025 appropriation (year of the law)]
properties.maintenance_cost: ≈ $52.5 million / ≈ €48.5 million a year in 2024 prices. Original: CBP budgets about $50–55 million a year for maintenance and repair (gates, roads, lighting, drainage, vegetation). An older OMB estimate gave at least $864,000 per mile per year. [midpoint of $50–55M a year; source year not given, assumed 2024]
properties.security_technology: Cameras, sensors and towers funded under the 2025 law. A partisan 2019-era estimate puts technology at about $1 million per mile. Border Patrol agents are not costed.
properties.purpose: Stated: stop illegal immigration and drug smuggling (US government).
properties.contractors: Wall construction, CBP awards 2017–2026 (USAspending, award values, which can be ceilings rather than spending): Barnard Construction ≈ $2.8 billion (3 awards); Fisher Sand & Gravel ≈ $2.2 billion (3); Southwest Valley Constructors ≈ $1.7 billion (1); SLS Federal Services ≈ $1.3 billion (1); BCCG joint venture ≈ $1.2 billion (2); Spencer Construction ≈ $0.9 billion (3); Barnard Spencer joint venture ≈ $0.7 billion (1); Granite Construction ≈ $0.5 billion (1); Sundt Construction ≈ $0.4 billion (1). Surveillance technology, CBP awards 2013–2026 (USAspending, award values): ElbitAmerica, Inc. (subsidiary of Elbit Systems; integrated fixed towers) ≈ $219 million (6 awards); General Dynamics One Source ≈ $213 million (remote video surveillance system upgrade, 2013); Anduril Industries ≈ $98 million (autonomous surveillance towers, 4 awards); GovPlace ≈ $21 million (autonomous towers); Meridian Engineering ≈ $19 million (integrated fixed tower site preparation); WSP USA ≈ $11 million (remote video surveillance); Teledyne FLIR ≈ $0.4 million.

properties.name: Calais port and Coquelles terminal fencing
properties.separates: Port of Calais and Eurotunnel terminal (UK border controls in France) / public road network
properties.owner: Port of Calais and Eurotunnel (French side); UK-funded
properties.construction: Double security fencing on the approach road, with gates and detection equipment (reported)
properties.note: Summer 2015 fencing funded by the UK government, after reports of migrants getting onto the Eurotunnel site. Reported lengths range from 2.5 km to 37 km; 2.5 km used here. Line joins the port and the Coquelles terminal, not a surveyed alignment.
properties.cost: ≈ $14.2 million / ≈ €12.2 million in 2024 prices. Original: £7 million for fencing at Coquelles, £2 million for a detection upgrade, £1 million for dog searching, £12 million for the juxtaposed border (UK government figures as reported). [£7M fencing at Coquelles, 2015]
properties.security_technology: Detection equipment, dog searches, gates and perimeter fencing.
properties.purpose: Stated: stop people getting onto the Eurotunnel site and port.

properties.name: Hadrian's Wall
properties.separates: Roman Britannia / peoples to the north (Caledonia)
properties.owner: Various UK heritage bodies (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
properties.construction: Stone wall in the east, turf wall in the west, with milecastles and turrets
properties.geometry_quality: partial (surviving segments traced in OpenStreetMap; the full route is not mapped)
properties.note: Begun in AD 122 and largely finished within about six years. Survives unevenly: best in the central hilly sector, little in the lowlands where stone was reused. Route shown is approximate; the documented length is 117 km. Drawn line covers only the surviving segments found in OpenStreetMap.
properties.purpose: Roman frontier defence against northern peoples.
properties.term_note: Historical: built as a frontier defence, no longer in use as a border. Surviving sections are standing.

properties.name: Great Wall of China (surviving sections)
properties.countries: China (Beijing, Hebei, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Ningxia, Gansu)
properties.separates: Chinese states and dynasties / northern steppe powers
properties.construction: Mainly stone and brick with watchtowers; rammed earth in the west (general description, not verified here)
properties.geometry_quality: traced (OpenStreetMap, simplified to about 50 m; surviving and partly ruined sections)
properties.note: Surviving sections of walls from several dynasties: Qin (from 221 BC), Han, Jin and Ming (1368–1644). The Ming wall is most of what survives. The documented Ming total of about 8,851 km includes trenches and natural barriers. Traced length is the sum of mapped sections.
properties.purpose: Ming frontier defence against northern steppe powers.
properties.term_note: Historical: built as a frontier defence, no longer in use as a border. Surviving sections are standing.

properties.name: Latvia–Russia border fence
properties.cost: ≈ $187.6 million / ≈ €166.0 million in 2024 prices. Original: €166 million total (reported Dec 2025), plus €20 million planned for patrol infrastructure [total at completion, Dec 2025]
properties.construction: Fence of about 280 km; construction type not confirmed in the sources
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full length; fenced portion not separated)
properties.note: Work from 2023 (start year approximate). Completed 30 Dec 2025. Length as reported at completion.
properties.security_technology: Patrol infrastructure and technology, €20 million planned.
properties.purpose: Stated: national security.

properties.name: Latvia–Belarus border fence
properties.cost: ≈ $135.7 million / ≈ €125.3 million in 2024 prices. Original: €125.35 million total, including €3.6 million from the EU [total, completed 2024]
properties.construction: Main fence of about 145 km; construction type not confirmed in the sources
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full length; fenced portion not separated)
properties.note: Section of 112 km completed 2023; main fence completed July 2024. Fenced portion not separated on the map.
properties.purpose: Stated: response to instrumentalised migration from Belarus.

properties.name: Bulgaria–Turkey border fence
properties.cost: ≈ $73.9 million / ≈ €64.3 million in 2024 prices. Original: About 100 million leva (about €51 million) by 2016; later reports approach 170 million leva (about €87 million) [100 million leva by 2016]
properties.construction: Fence topped with razor wire in places; height and type not confirmed in the sources
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full length; fenced portion not separated)
properties.note: Built without a public tender. Began with an 82 km section in 2014 and extended to about 230–270 km by 2017 (250 km used). Fenced portion not separated on the map.
properties.purpose: Stated: stop irregular migration.

properties.name: Hungary–Croatia border fence
properties.cost: Unknown (no source found for the Croatian section)
properties.construction: Fence with concertina wire; the 4 m height in the source may refer to the Serbian section
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full border line; fenced portion not separated)
properties.note: Fence work began 18 Sept 2015 and was reported complete along 348 km on 16 Oct 2015. Wikipedia says sections not separated by the Drava were fenced, but the source does not list them. Planned removal in early 2023 after Croatia joined Schengen; removal not confirmed. Earlier 41 km figure not supported by this source.
properties.purpose: Stated: stop migration during the 2015 crisis.
properties.term_note: Planned removal in early 2023 after Croatia joined Schengen; not confirmed.

properties.name: India–Pakistan border fence
properties.owner: Government of India (BSF; CPWD for roads)
properties.cost: ≈ $183.7 million / ≈ €147.8 million in 2024 prices. Original: Rs 2.4 million per km for fencing, about 2,091 km sanctioned (BSF figure, early 2000s).
properties.security_technology: Floodlights along the fence (2,079 km sanctioned, 2,044 km completed per government); patrol roads.
properties.construction: Fence with floodlights and patrol roads (steel fence in newer sections per government statements)
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full border line; fenced portion not separated)
properties.purpose: Stated: control cross-border terrorism, infiltration and smuggling (Indian government).
properties.contractors: Not identified in the sources (CPWD and BSF)
properties.note: Government figures date from 2003 to about 2022. Pakistani-side accounts were not found.

properties.name: Turkey–Iran border wall
properties.security_technology: Later phase: about 110 km of trenches and 103 fibre-optic 'smart' surveillance towers (reported).
properties.construction: Concrete modules about 3 m high and 2 m wide, with trenches
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full border line; wall covers only part of it)
properties.purpose: Stated: counter-terrorism (PKK) and smuggling; migration added as a reason from 2021.
properties.contractors: Not identified in the sources (TOKI reported for the Syria wall, not the Iran wall)
properties.note: 149 km completed by July 2021 (per reports). Construction start year approximate. Border about 295 km.

properties.name: Slovenia–Croatia border barrier
properties.cost: ≈ $33.6 million / ≈ €29.2 million in 2024 prices. Original: about €23.2 million installation (N1); about €31.5 million total on fences and surveillance, Nov 2015–2020 (Slovenia Times).
properties.maintenance_cost: About €3.6 million (reported, N1; year not given)
properties.security_technology: Related surveillance equipment included in the €31.5 million total (not itemised).
properties.construction: Wire mesh fence (about 145 km) and razor wire (51–85 km; sources differ)
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full border line; fenced sections not located)
properties.purpose: Stated: manage migration after the 2015–2016 crisis.
properties.term_note: Built as temporary barriers. Removal began 2022; by 10 Nov 2023, about 42 km of mesh and 27 km of razor wire removed. Final removal not confirmed.
properties.note: Length from the government's wire mesh figure; sources give different razor wire totals.

properties.name: Pakistan–Afghanistan border barrier
properties.cost: ≈ $680.8 million / ≈ €583.3 million in 2024 prices. Original: $532 million (VOA, 2017); Rs 10 billion for fencing, excluding detection system (The News, 2017).
properties.security_technology: Detection system (costed separately, not included); 443 forts planned, 150 built (The News).
properties.construction: Fence about 4 m high (Wikipedia)
properties.geometry_quality: official border (full border line; fenced sections not located)
properties.purpose: Stated: stop militant infiltration and terrorism; Wikipedia also lists drugs, arms, smuggling and irregular migration.
properties.note: Construction 2017 to December 2023 (Wikipedia). Afghanistan opposes the fence.

properties.name: Baghdad T-walls (blast walls)
properties.separates: Baghdad neighbourhoods and markets, sectarian lines
properties.cost: Unknown (a weak Wikipedia estimate of about $600 per wall, not verified)
properties.construction: Concrete T-walls about 3.66 m (12 ft) high
properties.purpose: Stated: break the cycle of sectarian violence; protect about 65 markets and about 50 neighbourhoods (US military).
properties.term_note: Partly removed by Iraqi authorities (about 30 km in six months, 2019, per Press TV); the rest not confirmed.
properties.note: Length is a secondary estimate: more than 100 km of T-wall (Kilcullen, via Modern War Institute); Sadr City alone about 48 km.

properties.name: West Bank barrier (concrete sections)
properties.note: Traced from OCHA's January 2018 layer. Constructed sections only; sections under construction or projected are not drawn. Sections are split by type.
properties.construction: Concrete wall, about 8–9 m high, mostly in urban areas (OCHA data, constructed sections)
properties.geometry_quality: official data (OCHA, West Bank Separation Barrier, Jan 2018; constructed sections only)
properties.cost: ≈ $4.50 billion / ≈ €3.86 billion in 2024 prices. Original: About $3.4 billion (2015 estimate); a 2012 estimate gives $2.6 billion for construction. [2015 estimate]
properties.maintenance_cost: ≈ $375.9 million / ≈ €322.7 million a year in 2024 prices. Original: About $260–284 million a year (2012 and 2015 estimates). [2015 estimate a year]
properties.security_technology: Electronic fence with sensors, a vehicle trench and a patrol road; concrete wall in urban areas. Guards not costed.
properties.purpose: Stated: prevent attacks from the West Bank (Israeli government).
properties.contractors: Elbit Systems (TORCH command system, per advocacy reports). Wall construction contractors not identified in the sources.

properties.security_technology: Trenches and control towers with infrared cameras (secondhand report, unverified)
properties.construction: Barbed-wire fence, trenches (secondary sources; not confirmed)
properties.geometry_quality: placeholder (area only; route not published, dot near the Oujda–Maghnia crossing)
